lines.title: A SMALL MODEL RAN 80× SLOWER
lines.narration_text: I read that a small model ran eighty times slower than a bigger one. So I made the arithmetic exactly equal, and went looking for where the time goes.

lines.title: WHAT IS A RECURRENT MODEL?
lines.narration_text: A recurrent model reads a sequence one step at a time, carrying a memory forward. I read that one of these ran far slower than a bigger model, and I wanted to see why.

lines.title: TWO MODELS, SAME WEIGHTS
lines.narration_text: So I built two tiny models with the same weights, the numbers a model learns. I'm Tanmay Kulkarni, in for Humanitarians AI.
lines.visual_intent: slate change: dissolve starts at 20.1 s; carried from the line before (on screen from the first frame): model container, first (amber), model container, second (teal), steps 1 2 3 chain; label 'first'; label 'second'; five rows (the second model); weight block, 'weights'; name chip: Tanmay K. · Humanitarians AI

lines.title: ONE WAITS, ONE DOES NOT
lines.narration_text: The first waits for itself. Every step needs the answer from the step before. The second has all its inputs up front, so it applies the same weights to every position at once.
lines.visual_intent: slate change: dissolve starts at 29.0 s; carried from the line before (on screen from the first frame): model container, first (amber), model container, second (teal), steps 1 2 3 chain, label 'first', label 'second', five rows (the second model), weight block, 'weights'; caption 'waits for itself'; caption 'applies the weights at once'; ring round the chain (with the thick arrows); ring round the rows
lines.status: persistent scene: what was on screen at the end of the line before is on screen from the first frame; new elements reveal in order

lines.title: SAME ARITHMETIC
lines.narration_text: Same weights. Over a hundred steps, twenty million operations each, an operation being one multiply and one add.

lines.title: TURN THE DIAL
lines.narration_text: Now a dial, for how much the chip can do at once. All the way down, one thing at a time. The first took six point one milliseconds. The second, six point four. The same.

lines.title: MORE OVERLAP
lines.narration_text: Turn it up. The second model can load a weight once and use it on many positions. The first cannot, because the next step has to wait. The first falls behind. One point three times slower. Then three point seven.
lines.visual_intent: slate change: dissolve starts at 57.7 s; carried from the line before (on screen from the first frame): model container, first (amber), model container, second (teal), steps 1 2 3 chain, label 'first', label 'second', five rows (the second model), weight block, 'weights', thick arrows between the steps (each waits for the last), the dial: ZERO, 8 ROWS, MATRIX UNIT; caption: loaded once, vs again each step; ring round MATRIX UNIT; bar 1.3× (first falls behind); bar 3.7×; the dial sweeps from ZERO to MATRIX UNIT
lines.status: persistent scene: what was on screen at the end of the line before is on screen from the first frame; new elements reveal in order

lines.title: WHY
lines.narration_text: The arithmetic never changed. What changed is how much work could happen together. The first model fetches its weights again on every single step.

lines.title: MY LAPTOP, NOT A CHIP
lines.narration_text: This is my laptop, not a small chip, and my gap is smaller than eighty. But it shows where the time can live: in the model and the chip together.

lines.title: THREE NUMBERS
lines.narration_text: Parameters tell you what a model stores. Operations tell you what it computes. Overlap tells you how long it waits.
